d6fa82aa-f741-47bd-a263-c0b6a9727a50#158.source:
When you create a table, you need to specify a name for the table (.dbf) file created to store the table. Both database tables and free tables require table file names. Table names must begin with a letter or underscore and can consist of letters, digits, or underscores.

If your table is in a database, you can specify a long table name, which can contain up to 128 characters, in addition to the table file name. You can use long table names instead of conventional file names to identify the table in a database more easily. Visual FoxPro displays long table names when the table appears in the Visual FoxPro interface, for example in the Project Manager, the Database Designer, the Query Designer, and the View Designer as well as in the title bar of a browse window.

> **Note:** If you remove a table from a database, the table retains its file name but not its long name.

- Open the database table in the Table Designer .
- In the Table Designer , click the Table tab.
- In the Name box, type a long name for the table.

- Include the NAME clause when creating a database table with the SQL CREATE TABLE command.

For more information, see Table Designer (Visual FoxPro) and CREATE TABLE - SQL Command.

You can rename the long names for database tables and the file names of database and free tables. You can rename the long names of database tables using the Table Designer because you are changing the long name, not the table file name. You can rename free tables only programmatically because free tables do not have long names.

- Open the database in the Database Designer .
- Find and make the table you want to rename active.
- On the Database menu, click Modify .
- In the Table Designer , click the Table tab.
- In the Name box, type a new name for the table.

For more information, see Database Designer (Visual FoxPro) and Table Designer (Visual FoxPro).

- Set the database containing the table you want to rename as the current database.
- Use the RENAME TABLE command.

For more information, see RENAME TABLE Command.

- Use the RENAME command. Caution Do not use the RENAME command on database tables. RENAME does not update the table's back link to the database and might cause errors when accessing the table. Use the RENAME TABLE command instead.

For more information, see RENAME Command.

Makes it possible for you to select fields.

When this dialog box opens by selecting Only fields specified by field filter and then clicking Field Filter in the Work Area Properties dialog box, this dialog box makes it possible for you to select fields that display or can be accessed in a browse window. Fields not chosen cannot be accessed, examined, or modified. However, data in the table is not affected. For more information, see Work Area Properties Dialog Box.

This dialog box appears when you click Field Filter in the Work Area Properties dialog box or Fields in the Quick Report Dialog Box, Append From Options Dialog Box, or Export Options Dialog Box.
 **All Fields**
Displays all field names in the current table.
**Selected Fields**
Displays field names you select in the All Fields box and copy with the Move button.
**From Table**
Specifies which table's fields are displayed in the All Fields box.
**Move**
Copies the selected fields from the All Fields box to the Selected Fields box.
**All**
Copies all fields from the All Fields box to the Selected Fields box.
**Remove**
Removes the selected fields from the Selected Fields box.
**Remove All**
Removes all fields from the Selected Fields box.

d771432f-0461-4062-8867-d9fc4db49a7a#158.source: The HTML Item dialog box is part of the Web Publishing wizard. This dialog box makes it possible for you to specify additional items and their attributes for the Web page you create.

To access the HTML Item dialog box
 - From Tools menu, choose Wizards , and then click Web Publishing .
- Navigate through the wizard until you reach Step 3.
- Click Advanced .
- In the Advanced dialog box, click Add .
 **Type**
This drop-down list provides a list of HTML tag items that you can add to your page.
**Location**
This drop-down list makes it possible for you to specify where on the Web page you want the selected HTML item to appear — in the header, before data, or after data.
**Text Formatting**
Text Specify the exact text you want to display in the location you selected in the Location drop-down list. Heading Specify, from the drop-down list, the HTML heading tag you want to apply to the specified text. Bold (Strong) Specify whether you want the specified text to be formatted bold. Italic Specify whether you want the specified text to be formatted italic. Font name Specify the font you want to use for the specified text. If you chose a Heading, then this option is disabled, and your Web page will use the heading value set in the viewing browser. Size Specify the font size you want to use for the specified text. If you chose a Heading, then this option is disabled, and your Web page will use the heading value set in the viewing browser. Alignment Specify the left-to-right page alignment of the specified HTML item. Forecolor Specify the foreground (default text) color of the specified HTML item. Backcolor Specify the color of the specified HTML item.
**Attributes**
File/HREF Specify or locate the file (or URL) you want to use if you chose Hyperlink or Image item in the Type drop-down list. Style Class Specify a path reference to a class contained in a cascading style sheet (.css).

When you click OK, you are returned to the Advanced dialog box where you can specify another HTML item, save the current data layout and style information, or proceed to Step 4 of the Web Publishing wizard.

This class loads and plays a video file, and provides access to the Media Control Interface (MCI).

| Category | Multimedia |

| Default Catalog | Visual FoxPro Catalog\Foundation Classes\Multimedia |
| Class | _videoplayer |
| Base Class | Container |

To use, drop the class on a project or form, or from the Component Gallery Item shortcut menu, select Add to Project or Add to Form. When you drop the class on a project, you can choose between adding the class or creating a subclass. When you choose an option from the shortcut menu or drop the class on a form, Visual FoxPro opens a builder so you can specify appropriate cFileName, lAutoOpen, lAutoPlay, lAutoRepeat, and cControlSource values.

See Guidelines for Using Visual FoxPro Foundation Classesfor more information on using foundation classes.

| Properties, Events, Methods | Description |
| --- | --- |
| AutoOpen property | Specifies whether the video file specified should be automatically opened when the class is created. Default: .T. |
| AutoPlay property | Specifies whether the video file should automatically play after opening. Default: .T. |
| AutoRepeat property | If true (.T.), specifies that the video file will play continuously. Default: .T. |
| cFileName property | Specifies the video file associated with the Video Frame. Default: "" |
| Controlsource property | Specifies the source of data to which an object is bound. Default: "" |
| MCIAlias property | Specifies the alias for the video file when calling MCI commands. If empty, the name of the file is used. Default: "" |
| MCIError property | Specifies the result of the last MCI command executed. Default: 0 |
| MCIErrorString property | Stores the error string from the last MCI command executed. Default: "" |
| CloseVideo method | Closes the video file and releases all resources. Syntax: CloseVideo( ) Return: none Arguments: none |
| DoMCI method | Executes an MCI command. Syntax: DoMCI(cMCIcmd) Return: cRetString Arguments: cMCIcmd specifies the command to run. |
| PauseVideo method | Pauses a currently playing video. Syntax: PauseVideo( ) Return: none Arguments: none |
| PlayVideo method | Plays the currently loaded video. Syntax: PlayVideo( ) Return: none Arguments: none |
| SetPosition method | Makes it possible for the user to set the position of the media file. Syntax: SetPosition(cPosition) Return: none Arguments: cPosition specifies Start, End, or a number representing milliseconds into the media file. |
| GetMCIError method | Internal to the class. |
| OpenVideo method | Internal to the class. |
| ShowMCIError method | Internal to the class. |

When you build a project, application, or dynamic-link library, Visual FoxPro includes build status and error messages in an error file, which is a text file with the .err file name extension, as they occur during the build process. The .err file has the same base name as your project and is created in the current directory. When you compile or recompile a project, application, or dynamic-link library, compile messages are also included in the same .err file.

If the build process is interrupted, you can open the .err file to review these messages. You can also select the Display Errors option in the Build Options dialog box to display an editing window for the .err file after the build process completes so you can review any errors.

> **Note:** If no errors occur during the build, the .err file is removed.

During the build process, build status messages appear in the status bar. After the build process completes, the number of build errors appear in the status bar.

- Build the project, application, or dynamic-link library file by following the steps in How to: Test a Project or How to: Build Applications .
- To display the error file automatically after the build process completes, when the Build Options dialog box is open, select the Display Errors check box. -OR- To view the error file after the build process completes, on the Project menu, choose Errors .

For more information, see Build Options Dialog Box.

You can also specify whether to include compile messages by using the SET LOGERRORS command. For more information, see SET LOGERRORS Command.

You can also view and save build status messages that appear in the Debug Output window when it is open in the Debugger. For more information, see Debug Output Window and Debugger Window.

- Build the project, application, or dynamic-link library file by following the steps in How to: Test a Project or How to: Build Applications , respectively.
- In the Build Options dialog box, select the Recompile All Files check box.

d8915fa8-336d-4dff-9055-38970910c018#159.source:
Sets the foreground or background buffer memory size.

```foxpro
SYS(3050, nType, [nBuffMemSize])
```

**nType**
Specifies the buffer. The following table lists the values for nType and the corresponding buffer: nType Buffer 1 Foreground 2 Background
**nBuffMemSize**
Specifies the maximum buffer memory size in bytes. If you specify a value for nBuffMemSize that is less than 256K bytes, Visual FoxPro sets the buffer memory size to 256K bytes. Specify 0 for nBuffMemSize to return the buffer memory size to the Visual FoxPro startup value. The startup value depends on the amount of your computer's memory. If you omit nBuffMemSize , SYS(3050) returns the buffer memory size for the buffer specified with nType.

SYS(3050) makes it possible for you to optimize Visual FoxPro performance by adjusting the amount of memory Visual FoxPro allocates for the foreground and background buffers. The foreground memory buffer is the memory available to Visual FoxPro when it is operating in the foreground as the currently active application. The background memory buffer is the memory available to Visual FoxPro when it is operating in the background when another application is the foreground application.

SYS(3050) returns a numeric value as a character string that indicates the maximum amount of memory Visual FoxPro allocates for the foreground or background buffers.

d8a9edcb-8b65-422d-8c4c-a21f41742e4e#159.source: When you coordinate a menu with a toolbar, the menu items accomplish the same tasks as the associated toolbar buttons, and the menu items are automatically disabled when the associated toolbar button is disabled.

- In the Menu and Shortcut Designers , create a submenu with a descriptive prompt for every button on the toolbar.
- In the result column for each submenu item, choose Command .
- For each submenu item, call the code associated with the Click Event of the appropriate toolbar command button. For example, if the name of the button on the toolbar is cmdA , add the following line of code in the edit box for the submenu item command: Formset.toolbar.cmdA.Click
- Choose the button in the Options column to open the Prompt Options dialog box and choose Skip For .
- In the Expression Builder Dialog Box , enter an expression that indicates that the menu option should be skipped when the toolbar command button is not enabled. For example, if the name of the button on the toolbar is cmdA , enter the following expression in the Skip For box: NOT formset.toolbar.cmdA.Enabled
- Generate the menu.
- Add the menu to the form set with the toolbar and run the form set.

When the user opens the menu, Visual FoxPro evaluates the Skip For condition, disabling the menu item if the associated toolbar command button is disabled. When the user chooses an item on the menu, the code in the Click Event of the associated toolbar command button is executed.
